newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - No cut in Swedish repo rate this week.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - No cut in Swedish repo rate this week.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, will probably keep its key repo rate at an unchanged fixed 4.95 percent at its regular tender on Tuesday, a poll of economists and analysts showed on Monday.
Nine of eleven market players polled said the Riksbank would leave the rate unchanged while two said the central bank would cut the rate, which it lowered by 10 basis points on October 8.
"There is a good chance they will lower the rate again tomorrow. The Riksbank's latest comments point to this," said one analyst who believes the bank would cut the rate.
The Riksbank's move last week fitted into the bank's pattern in recent months of cutting the rate every other week, with the most recent cuts all of 10 basis points.

Deputy Riksbank governor Lars Heikensten said last week the Riksbank did not necessarily have to follow a certain pattern in the future, a comment which has caused some confusion on the market according to analysts.
Some said it was a sign the bank would not cut the rate in the same pattern while others said it showed the bank planned to cut rates more aggressively than before.
The repo rate, which began the year at 8.91 percent, is the central rate in a three tier system and the bank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity.
